The search didn't turn up a clear arXiv RAG evaluation paper from 2026. It did surface these 2026 benchmarks:

- **LIT-RAGBench** (LREC 2026, Itai et al.) targets the generator side of RAG. It tests whether a generator can combine evidence from long contexts, reason across steps, read tables, and abstain when evidence is missing. Its authors note that existing benchmarks don't test several of these capabilities together under one setup. Anthology ID 2026.lrec-main.427 is the entry for it.
- **MTRAGEval** is a SemEval-2026 Task 8 benchmark for multi-turn RAG. It covers passage retrieval, grounded response generation, and end-to-end RAG across four English domains: ClapNQ, Cloud, FiQA, and Govt. Its citation traces to a March 2026 paper, per Athanasiou et al., 11 Mar 2026. Its scoring uses retrieval metrics such as nDCG@K along with abstention handling.

For older but foundational work, RGB (arXiv 2309.01431) evaluates LLMs on noise robustness, negative rejection, information integration, and counterfactual robustness. It is from 2023, not 2026.

content.text:
Here are three recent papers on evaluating RAG systems. I took them from search results and didn't open the papers, so check details against the originals.

1. **LIT-RAGBench: Benchmarking Generator Capabilities of Large Language Models in Retrieval-Augmented Generation** (LREC 2026, Itai et al.). It evaluates the generator side of RAG. It tests whether a model can combine evidence from long contexts, reason across steps, read tables, and abstain when the evidence is missing. Its authors say existing benchmarks don't test these together. [Link](https://preview.aclanthology.org/ingest-lrec/2026.lrec-main.427/)

2. **MTRAGEval (SemEval-2026 Task 8)**. This is a benchmark for multi-turn RAG. It covers passage retrieval, grounded response generation, and end-to-end RAG across four English domains (ClapNQ, Cloud, FiQA, Govt). Scoring uses retrieval metrics such as nDCG@K and also handles abstention. The search results tied it to a March 2026 paper by Athanasiou et al., but I only saw a topic page for it, not the paper. [Link](https://api.emergentmind.com/topics/mtrageval)

3. **Benchmarking Large Language Models in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RGB)** (arXiv 2309.01431). This one is from 2023, so it isn't recent. I included it because it is the foundational benchmark the newer work builds on. It tests noise robustness, negative rejection, information integration, and counterfactual robustness. [Link](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2309.01431)

If you need three papers all from 2025–2026, I can run a more targeted search for a third one.

- [LIT-RAGBench](https://preview.aclanthology.org/ingest-lrec/2026.lrec-main.427/)
- [MTRAGEval](https://api.emergentmind.com/topics/mtrageval)
- [RGB benchmark](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2309.01431)
